purpose: Prototype v7: the path trap of the third work (human against machine, decision 3 of .steering/20261031-keystroke-concept), as the study of paper B. Main question (decision 1 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-literature; reworded by amendment A1): whether human-versus-machine judgments from keystroke timing respond to replaying a series through the input path and loggers, on the human side (a person's recorded series against the same gaps replayed) and on the machine side (a machine's planned schedule against the same schedule recorded through the path). It is not a question of what share of a discrimination is due to the path. Human records of KUPA-KEYS are replayed on one machine through the same path and loggers as several machines (constant, LLM token times, LLM-planned gaps, draws from human gaps); the researcher's own live typing on that machine and its replay separate the deformation added by the replay system. Headline test (decision 4 of the same folder; extended by amendments A2, B4): five detectors re-implemented from published descriptions (Condrey 2026's rule and two classifiers on its features; QUACK!-type, Lotto et al. 2026; a reduced BeCAPTCHA-Type, DeAlcala et al. 2023), set up without the path, judge the replayed human series against the original (human side) and each machine's plan against its recording (machine side); the paired change of the judgments is read per detector, layer and side. Secondary: the LLM's own timing (token arrival, planned gaps) measured through the path.

series.M1_8B and M1_14B: token arrival times: each model, 40 prompts (P1-P40) x 1 seed (seed 1) (amendment B1, decisions 9 and 13 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline: 40 independent clusters instead of 10), temperature 0.7, stream. Characters counted as Unicode code points after NFC; an empty token is skipped and counted. Causal schedule [the rule of this sentence is replaced by amendment B13 below]: with a_k the arrival of token k and n_k its characters, the characters of token k (k >= 2) are planned at a_k + j * (a_k - a_{k-1}) / n_k, j = 0..n_k-1 (spread over the previous inter-arrival interval); token 1 waits for token 2 and is spread over a_2 - a_1. Times are relative to a_1. (amendment B13, decision 33, replacing B12's raise to the determination time, which put token 1 and token 2's first character all at a_2) The schedule is delayed by one token: the characters of token k are wished at a_{k+1} + j * (a_{k+1} - a_k) / n_k, j = 0..n_k-1, where a_{K+1} is the end of generation for the last token K; every character is thus wished no earlier than it is determined, with no special case for token 1. This replaces the rule above ('k >= 2 at a_k + ..., token 1 waits for token 2'). (amendment B11, decision 22) These are the wished times; they can go backwards (a token that arrives early is planned before the end of the previous token). The executable plan is their running maximum (the character order kept; equal times allowed), and it is the plan of the machine side. (amendment B14, decision 36) The executable plan is not cleaned: its equal times (zero gaps, made by the running maximum wherever the wished times go backwards) are kept as the machine's plan, the share of planned presses with a zero gap is reported per series, and the ties-kept sensitivity (analysis_details.sensitivity_cleaning) is applied to the plan side as well; M1 stays in the machine-side general statement. (amendment B6) A press whose planned time is earlier than the previous press's sent time waits (queue; no skipping, no catching up faster than the schedule); its sent time is the later of its planned time and the moment the previous press was sent; the queue length and the wait (sent minus planned) of each press are recorded. Five times are kept apart for every press: the wished time, the executable plan (before any wait), the sent time, and the recorded time on each layer; the difference of the wished time and the executable plan is reported apart (the share of presses moved and their median shift). The wait belongs to the path side, not to the machine's plan. Typed while generating.

pairs.typer: H1_idle against M0, M1, M2, M3a, M3b (same path and loggers)
pairs.plan_execution: M2: planned gaps against recorded gaps
pairs.replay_error: for every replayed series (H1, L1, M1_replay, M2, M3, P): recorded minus planned, reported separately as offset (median), jitter (MAD and 95th percentile of the absolute deviation from the offset), drops (planned presses not recorded), order inversions, and cumulative drift (recorded minus planned time of the last press)
pairs.replay_repeat: H1_idle against H1_rep (10 persons): the system's replay-to-replay variability, read on continuous quantities only (amendment A3): the gap-level deviation of the two recordings (offset, jitter and drift as in replay_error, with H1_idle's recorded times in the place of the planned ones) and the per-person paired difference of the scores (D1 delta, D2, D3 and D4 'machine' probability); flips b and c are reported as counts with no equivalence reading (n = 10 gives Tango's interval [-0.278, 0.278] even with no flip). This floor is read beside H0 against H1: a headline 'responds' is described as above the floor only if, on the same 10 persons, the 95% bootstrap interval over persons of the mean of |score(H1_idle) - score(H0)| - |score(H1_rep) - score(H1_idle)| lies above 0 (numpy key [20261031, 7, 12, layer, detector]); with fewer than 8 complete triplets the floor is not read
pairs.quantisation_only: H0 against H0q: timing quantisation and jitter alone, without any replay
pairs.machine_path: (amendment A2) each machine series' planned times, never passed through any path (M0: the constant schedule; M1_8B and M1_14B: the executable plan before any wait (amendments B6, B11; the waits are counted on the path side and reported apart); M1_replay: the same executable plan; M2: the LLM's plan as validated; M3a and M3b: the drawn gaps), against the same series as recorded on each layer: the machine-side counterpart of H0 against H1_idle (the contrast differs: the human side is system A against replay plus system B, the machine side is no system against a system). The planned series pass through no system of this study; (amendment B11) M3a and M3b redraw KUPA's recorded gaps and so carry KUPA's grid and recording, while M0, M1 and M2 carry none.
pairs.hook: (amendment B11) P_nohook against the same controls of P without load, on the page layer: the median and the jitter (MAD, 95th percentile of the absolute deviation from the offset) of the recorded gaps, described.

resolution: effective resolution by Monaco 2016's method (spacing of peaks of the press-press histogram) on H0 of the 80 persons (amendment B11), on H1 and on P, per layer
stages_C1: v6's stages S0 (7 quantiles of ln gap), S1 (median and IQR of p and q over sentence tiles), S2 (median and IQR of depth and fineness) per series. Human-versus-machine per pair of the 'typer' and 'path' rows: out-of-fold scores of logistic regression (C 1, StandardScaler, 5 folds grouped by connected components of the relation 'shares a person (H0, H1, the E donor of M3), a text (M0, M3 and M1_8B share texts) or a prompt and seed' so that no related series fall in two folds, numpy key [20261031, 7, 4, layer, pair, stage]); rank_auc of the scores with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples of persons/texts; read on v6's two axes (decisions 4 and 8 of .steering/20261031-compression-audit-v6: lower end above 0.5 'detectable'; upper end below 0.60 'below 0.60', lower end above 0.60 'above 0.60', else 'undecided').

detectors_C2.decision: decision 5: Condrey and QUACK!-type, re-implemented from the papers (verified wording in .steering/20261102-paper-b-literature/verify.md and decisions.md of .steering/20261102-v7-conditions). (amendment B4) D4 adds a reduced version of the peer-reviewed BeCAPTCHA-Type; Gonzalez et al. 2022 (Systems and Soft Computing) is not used: its liveness detector compares a user's samples with forgeries built from that user's own profile and key names, which one essay per person cannot provide. Kundu 2024 and Mehta 2026 are not used: they separate a person's own writing from a person's transcription and do not judge machine typing.
detectors_C2.D1: Condrey's rule: delta = SD (ddof 0) / mean of the session's gaps after one pass removing gaps above 10 x the mean of all gaps; 'human' if delta > 0.269, else 'machine'. No training.
detectors_C2.D2: Condrey's seven features (delta; mean gap; gap variance; share of gaps > 500 ms; mean length of runs of consecutive gaps < 150 ms; Shannon entropy (natural log) of a 50-bin histogram on [0, 2000] ms, gaps above 2000 ms left out of the histogram and counted; SD of differences of consecutive gaps), trim as D1; logistic regression (C 1) and random forest (100 trees), StandardScaler, seed 42; trained on H0 of E (human) against equally many synthetic sessions with gaps ~ Uniform(30, 80) ms of matched length, never passed through any path. 'machine' if probability > 0.5.
detectors_C2.D3: QUACK!-type: windows of 70 consecutive gaps; features per window the 70 gaps and J_t = |gap_t - gap_{t-1}| (J_0 = 0) flattened (hold omitted: decision 6, a departure from the paper); random forest of 300 trees, otherwise scikit-learn defaults, seed 123; trained with each session weighted equally (window weight 1 / its session's number of windows) on all non-overlapping windows of H0 of E against equally many windows from three generators fitted on H0 of E without any path (uniform between the pooled 1st and 99th percentiles; empirical resampling of pooled gaps; 8-bin conditional resampling as M3b, pooled), one third each. Session score: mean probability over its non-overlapping windows; 'machine' if > 0.5. Sessions with fewer than 70 gaps get no D3 score and are counted.
detectors_C2.D4: (amendment B4, decision 17 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline) a reduced version of BeCAPTCHA-Type (DeAlcala et al., CVPR Workshops 2023; the peer-reviewed bot detector that set the question), not the original: the paper's detectors use five features per keystroke (hold, inter-press, inter-release, inter-key latencies and the key code) on the first L = 30 keystrokes and state no classifier settings and no input layout, so only the inter-press latency f2 can be built from press-press gaps (verified wording in .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline/round3/detector-28-becaptcha.md). Features: the first 30 press-press gaps of a session, as they are (no scaling). Synthetic sessions as the paper's Universal model: a Gaussian KDE (bandwidth 1.0 ms; the paper states sigma = 1.0 without a unit) of the pooled first 30 gaps of every training session of H0 of E that holds at least 30 gaps (amendment B10: a shorter session has no first 30 gaps), each synthetic gap drawn independently (a draw below 0 is drawn again and counted), one synthetic session of 30 gaps per such training human session, never passed through any path (the paper builds times from hold and inter-key draws; here gaps are drawn directly, a departure). Classifier: random forest of 100 trees, otherwise scikit-learn defaults, seed 28 (of the paper's four binary classifiers, RF was better than SVM in its user-dependent setting; the LSTM's best results used key codes, which are not replayed). Training generator numpy.random.default_rng(28). 'machine' if the probability > 0.5. Sessions with fewer than 30 gaps get no D4 score and are counted. Checked by the same validity gate (fold k: training synthetic from default_rng([28, k + 1]), held-out synthetic from default_rng([28, k + 1, 1]) (amendment B10), the KDE fitted on the training folds only; one held-out synthetic session per held-out human session with at least 30 gaps).
detectors_C2.count: per layer, detector and series: the share of sessions judged 'machine'; for H0, H1, L0, L1 (independent sessions) with a 95% Clopper-Pearson interval; for machine series that share texts or donors with a 95% interval over 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples of texts (numpy key [20261031, 7, 5, layer, detector, series]). For the paired rows (H0 against H1_idle and H1_load, H1_idle against H1_rep, H0 against H0q, L0 against L1; for H1_idle against H1_rep and L0 against L1 Tango's interval is reported only and never read, amendment B9): the counts of flips human->machine (b) and machine->human (c), the paired difference (b - c) / n with Tango's 95% score interval, and the mean change of the 'machine' probability (D2, D3, D4) with a 95% bootstrap interval over persons. (amendment A4) The paired change of the score is counted for every detector and paired row and reported beside the headline in the same table: D1 the change of delta, D2, D3 and D4 the change of the 'machine' probability, each the mean with a 95% bootstrap interval over persons (pairs with a missing score removed and counted), descriptive with no margin. Each detector's margin to its threshold on H0 (the distribution of delta - 0.269 for D1 and of 0.5 - probability for D2, D3 and D4) is reported beside. (amendment A2) For the machine_path rows: b, c and n per detector, layer and machine series, the paired difference (b - c) / n and the discordance (b + c) / n with 95% percentile intervals over 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples (clusters: texts for M0 and M1_replay, prompts for M1 and M2, donors for M3a and M3b; numpy key [20261031, 7, 11, layer, detector, series] with layer and detector as in analysis_details.keys and series 0 M0, 1 M1_8B, 2 M1_14B, 3 M1_replay of 8B, 4 M1_replay of 14B, 5 M2_8B, 6 M2_14B, 7 M3a, 8 M3b), and the paired score change with the same cluster bootstrap. (amendment B9) Saturation: for D2, D3 and D4, the share of sessions with a 'machine' probability at most 0.01 or at least 0.99 is reported in every row, and for D2_lr the paired change is also reported on the logit (its decision function) beside the probability. (amendment B9) The scaling of b and c to the effective n: b_eff = b * n_eff / n and c_eff = c * n_eff / n, substituted into Tango's and Wilson's intervals without rounding (example: 40 sessions in 34 clusters with b = 1, c = 0 gives b_eff = 0.85).
detectors_C2.headline: two-sided equivalence (decision 10, the researcher): per detector and layer, the paired difference of the 'machine' share between H1_idle and H0. Tango's interval inside [-0.10, 0.10] and the upper end of the 95% Wilson interval of the discordance (b + c) / n at most 0.10 -> 'the judgment is not changed by this replay and recording beyond 0.10'; (amendment B3, decision 10 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline: 'responds' in two steps) the whole of Tango's interval outside [-0.10, 0.10] (both ends on the same side beyond the margin), or the lower end of the discordance's Wilson interval above 0.10 (amendment A5: flips in both directions that cancel in the difference) -> 'responds beyond 0.10'; else 'undecided'. Reported beside the reading in every cell: 'changed from 0' if Tango's interval excludes 0 (it can stand with 'undecided', when the interval excludes 0 and straddles a margin). The route (difference, discordance or both) is given for 'responds beyond 0.10' only. Before B3 an interval that excluded 0 with one end beyond 0.10 read 'responds', which did not show a change beyond 0.10 (b = 4, c = 0 read 'responds'), and narrowing the interval could turn 'responds' into 'undecided'. Flips b and c are reported beside it in every cell. Design calculation (amendment B11: n = 80; before B11 n = 40 read 'not changed' only with no flip): b = c = 0 gives [-0.046, 0.046]; one flip [-0.034, 0.067]; two flips one way [-0.022, 0.087] or one each way [-0.057, 0.057] (discordance's Wilson [0.007, 0.087]), all 'not changed'; three flips one way [-0.010, 0.105], 'undecided'. The level 95% (0.025 on each side) is kept as the conservative side: with 90% three flips would read 'not changed' ([0.004, 0.090]). The margin 0.10 is tied to the validity gate's tolerance for held-out humans judged 'machine' (0.10): a change of replay and recording that moves more humans than the gate tolerates is read as a response. (amendment B3) This reason concerns the direction human -> machine (b); the same margin is applied to the direction machine -> human (c) and to the machine rows symmetrically, because no reason fixed before any value supports a different margin by direction or side. (amendment B11, decision 19) The probabilities of the three readings for one cell under true flip rates of 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20 and 0.30 (half each way) are computed from the design (no data) and reported in the supplement, with bounds for the general statement over the human side's 10 cells assuming independence (cells share persons, so this is a rough bound) [replaced by amendment B12 below: the Frechet bounds; the product is an example, not a bound]. Near the margin the reading is mostly 'undecided' (n = 80, rate 0.10: 'undecided' about 0.96). When a cell reads 'undecided', what is said of it is the flips b and c and the paired score change, described. The machine_path rows are read by the same rule (amendment A2) on two pairs of intervals separately: their cluster bootstrap intervals, and Tango's (difference) and Wilson's (discordance) intervals computed with the number of clusters as the effective n and b, c scaled to it; the row reads their common reading and 'undecided' if they disagree, so that a rare flip or a few clusters cannot read 'not changed' more easily than on the human side (one flip of 40 sessions reads 'undecided'), and no reading is created by combining them. Both readings are reported. Cluster sizes are unequal (a limit: neither interval guarantees its coverage under strong imbalance); sessions are weighted equally in the bootstrap; the route of a 'responds' (difference, discordance or both) is reported. Interval ends equal to 0.10 are inside (closed bounds). The design table holds for one cell with independent persons and one flip rate; it is not carried to the clustered machine rows or to all cells together. Scope: the reading is about responding to this change of replay and recording conditions, not about 'the path' in general, and H1_rep sets the floor of replay-to-replay change. Across detectors and layers: 'not changed' is claimed for a detector only on the layers where it reads so; (amendment B11, decision 26, as analysis_details.across) a general statement 'these detectors' judgments are not changed beyond 0.10 by this change of replay and recording conditions' (amendment B12: the Scope's words, not 'this path') requires all five detectors to be valid and every one on both layers to read 'not changed' (if any detector is 'not valid here', no general statement is made; the cells of the valid ones are still read one by one); 'responds beyond 0.10' for any valid detector on either layer is reported as such. (amendment B8) A general statement on the machine side covers only the machine series whose effective number of clusters can read 'not changed' with no flip (35 or more: 34 gives Tango's [-0.102, 0.102] at b = c = 0); a series with fewer (for instance M2 after six or more failed prompts, or sessions removed for missing judgments [amendment B14 below: a missing judgment is a missing pair, which keeps the series out by the bounds, not by the clusters]) is described and does not enter it. The design table of the supplement gives, for n_eff from 10 to 40, the zero-flip intervals and readings, and for each machine series its planned number of clusters (M0, M1, M1_replay, M2, M3a, M3b: 40) and how many lost clusters it can bear (5) [amendment B14: lost clusters are sessions without a plan, not missing pairs; see below]. (amendment B11, decision 23) Missing data: for every series the failures are reported with the planned sessions as the denominator, apart for failed generation, failed capture and no judgment; and every reading is reported beside two bounds that place the missing pairs as no flips and as flips (all one way, b, and all the other way, c) [three bounds in all, no flips, all b and all c, as amendment B12 counts them; amendment B14 below says which missing data they place back]. The machine series that enter the machine-side general statement are those with at least 35 clusters in every cell, fixed by B8; a series kept out is listed with its readings and not stated about. On the human side, a cell with fewer than 35 complete pairs enters no general statement either. (amendment B11, decision 25) A detector whose gridded validity version (validity_gate) has an AUC below 0.90 carries the note 'possible dependence on the recording grid' (amendment B12, decision 30: on every one of its cells whatever the reading; 'grid dependence unknown' on every cell when the gridded AUC is unknown; each 'responds beyond 0.10' cell of the human side is shown beside the same detector's flips from H0 to H0q, quantisation and jitter alone): H1 inherits KUPA's grid, so a detector leaning on the grid is not moved by the replay either. (amendment B12, decision 29) A cell enters the general statement, and 'not changed' is said in the abstract, only if its complete-pair reading and all three missing-data bounds read 'not changed'; a cell whose bounds disagree keeps its complete-pair reading with the note 'split by missing data'. (amendment B12) The bounds on the probability of the human side's general statement are the Frechet bounds, max(0, sum of the cell probabilities - 9) and the smallest cell probability, with the product under independence shown as an example, not a bound. The design table also gives the three probabilities when all flips go one way (b only). (amendment B14, decision 35) Missing data are of two kinds. A session without a plan (an M2 prompt that fails 3 attempts, an M1 generation that fails, a donor or text that cannot be drawn) is outside the pairs: it lowers the effective number of clusters and is what B8's 'lost clusters it can bear (5)' counts. A pair whose plan or original exists but whose capture failed, or that has no judgment, is a missing pair, and only missing pairs are placed back by the three bounds. Decision 29 is kept: on the machine side one missing pair placed as a flip reads 'undecided' (one flip of 40), so a machine series with any missing pair in a cell enters no general statement; on the human side, with no other flip, at most 2 missing pairs leave the one-way bounds 'not changed' (b + m <= 2 at n = 80). The design table gives, beside the three probabilities, the probability that a cell enters the general statement with m = 0, 1 and 2 missing pairs. (amendment B14, decision 37) The H0 to H0q flips shown beside a human-side 'responds beyond 0.10' cell are those of the two jitter versions of sensitivity_quantisation (SD 2 ms and 8 ms), both shown; its grid versions and the KUPA-resolution version are described in the supplement only, the latter 'unknown' when no resolution is read.
detectors_C2.validity_gate: before the headline is read: within E, 5 folds by person (numpy key [20261031, 7, 8]); D2, D3 and D4 trained on 4 folds with their synthetic generators fitted on those folds only; AUC on the held-out persons against held-out synthetic sessions from the same generators, and the share of held-out humans judged 'machine'. A detector whose held-out AUC is below 0.90 or whose held-out human 'machine' share exceeds 0.10 is reported as 'not valid here' and its headline is not read as robustness. D1 is checked in the same way with no training. (amendment B5, decision 12 of .steering/20261102-paper-b-outline; descriptive) The held-out human sessions carry KUPA's recording grid while the synthetic sessions are continuous, so a detector could pass the gate by the grid alone. Beside the gate, the same trained detectors are scored on the held-out synthetic sessions with their press times rounded to KUPA's effective resolution estimated from H0 of E (resolution; amendment B12, decision 30: if no resolution is read, the gridded version is not computed and its AUC is 'unknown', never 1 ms), and the AUC and the held-out human 'machine' share of this gridded version are reported. They do not decide validity. (amendment B11) The gate's E is E_train (E without the 40 M3 donors).

sensitivity_quantisation: the machine series' recorded press times (not gaps) with the original system's timing added under several assumptions, each separately, gaps recomputed after: rounding times to a 1 ms, 4 ms and 16 ms grid; Gaussian jitter SD 2 ms and 8 ms on each time; KUPA's effective resolution estimated from H0 (resolution). C1 and C2 recomputed; whether each reading changes is reported. H0q applies the same to H0.
prediction: Claude's, written before any value; each item passes or fails on its own. (P1) hook layer: |recorded median gap - planned| <= 1 ms for every control without load. (P2) browser layer: <= 2 ms for 18, 50, 100, 200 ms without load. (P3) the 5 ms control is the only control with a share of recorded browser gaps below 1 ms above 0.05. (P4) load moves no control's median by more than 2 ms on either layer. (R1) H1_idle replay error: 95th percentile of absolute deviation from the offset below 5 ms (hook) and below 10 ms (browser); |cumulative drift| below 50 ms per essay. (V1) every detector passes the validity gate. (Hd1) D1 headline 'not changed' on both layers (b = c = 0: human delta near 1 is far above 0.269). (Hd2) D2, D3 and D4 (D4 added by amendment B4) headline 'not changed' on both layers. (Hd3, amended A3) H1_idle against H1_rep: 95th percentile of the absolute gap deviation below 2 ms (hook) and 5 ms (browser), and (amendment B9) (amendment B11, decision 24) for every detector, with at least 8 complete pairs (else not read, amendment B12), the mean over persons of the absolute per-person paired change at most 0.02 (a point estimate, Claude's prediction; on delta, whose human values lie near 1, 0.02 is about 2% of the scale, and on probabilities 2 points; not derived from a cost; the share of saturated probabilities is shown beside it, since saturated scores meet it trivially), on delta for D1 and on the 'machine' probability for D2_lr, D2_rf, D3 and D4; the signed mean is reported as the bias with its 95% percentile bootstrap interval over persons (key of analysis_details.keys, pair 2) and does not decide (with 10 persons the percentile interval tends to be narrow, a limit). (Hm1, A2) machine side: D1 keeps M0 'machine' in 40 of 40 from plan to record on both layers (amendment B7: nearly by construction, since M0's delta is near 0 and a few ms of jitter cannot lift it to 0.269; not counted as support for the detectors' robustness). (Hm2, amended B7, B11) M3a and M3b: from plan to record, every detector (all five valid, analysis_details.across) on both layers reads 'not changed' (which needs b = c = 0 with at least 35 clusters). No prediction for the machine side of M1 and M2. (Dm1) D1 judges M0 'machine' in 40 of 40; M3a and M3b 'human' in at least 38 of 40; M1_8B and M1_14B 'machine' in at least 30 of 40. No prediction for M2. (Dm2) D3 judges M3b 'human' in more sessions than M3a. (C1a) H0 against H1_idle at S0: 'below 0.60' or 'undecided' on both layers. (C1b) H1_idle against M0 and against M1 (each model) at S0: 'above 0.60'. (C1c) H1_idle against M3a and M3b at S1 and S2: not 'above 0.60'. (G1, amended A6) the share of gaps below 40 ms (the first bin of the 50-bin histogram on [0, 2000] ms) differs between H0 and H1_idle by more than 0.01, and no other bin of that histogram does. Not being able to read 'not changed' (undecided) is not counted as support for 'harmless'. (P5, amendments B11, B12) for 18 and 50 ms (and 5 ms, amendment B14) without load, on the page layer, P_nohook against P with the hook: the median recorded gap within 1 ms (a constant hook delay cancels in gaps, so this part is nearly trivial), the MAD and the 95th percentile of the absolute deviation from the offset each within 1 ms, and the share of recorded gaps below 1 ms within 0.01. If P5 fails, every page-layer reading is stated for the configuration with the hook installed. (amendment B14) If P5 passes, what is said is that on these three controls without load the hook did not move the page layer beyond the limits; the page-layer readings are still stated for the configuration with the hook installed.
limits_written_before: One machine, one OS, one browser, two loggers; software injection only (no physical key presses, no robot), so the path studied is a software path. H0 was logged by a browser keylogger on each person's own machine and H1 on the work PC: H0 against H1 mixes the change of system with the replay system, and only L0 against L1 isolates the replay system, with one typist (the researcher) and 4 essays. No new human data are collected beyond the researcher's own. Only counted presses are replayed; holds are not measured, so the QUACK!-type detector departs from the paper. The detectors are re-implementations from the papers' text, not the authors' code; D4 is a reduced version of BeCAPTCHA-Type on press-press gaps only, with classifier settings fixed by us (amendment B4), and its results are not those of the original detector; Condrey's gap definition is not stated in the paper and press-press is used. LLM results are for two local models with fixed prompts and are not a claim about LLMs in general. Readings are descriptive; no correction for multiple comparisons. H0 against H1 does not separate the contribution of the path from the change of machine and logger (it is their sum); L0 against L1 is on the same machine and loggers and isolates the replay system, but with one typist and 4 essays it is described on gaps and scores only (amendment B9). The readings are limited to 'responds to this change of replay and recording conditions'. The machine side (planned against recorded) and the human side are reported beside each other; no combined test of 'equal effect on both conditions' is made. The planned machine series carry no quantisation while H0 carries KUPA's, so the two sides are not symmetric in their starting point (sensitivity_quantisation is the check). The software path is not a physical keyboard, USB or HID: perturbations of firmware and USB polling are outside it. The replay persons are English learners' essays with at least 300 counted presses. The equivalence margin 0.10 (eight persons in 80 net after amendment B11) is a judgment of a practically small change, not derived from a cost [its kind is stated by amendment B14 below: set by the sample available and tied to the validity gate's tolerance]. (amendment B9) H1_rep's 10 persons give percentile bootstrap intervals that tend to be narrow. The machine rows' clusters (prompts, texts, donors) are 40 each by design; lost clusters (failures, missing judgments) can remove a series from the general statement (B8) [amendment B14: sessions without a plan lower the clusters; a missing judgment or capture is a missing pair and keeps the series out through the bounds]. (amendment B11) The page layer is recorded with the OS hook installed, as in no deployment; P_nohook checks this on two controls only [three controls, 5, 18 and 50 ms, by amendment B14]. H1 and M3 inherit KUPA's recording grid. The non-integer b_eff and c_eff substituted into Tango's and Wilson's intervals are an approximation by an effective sample size, not a standard procedure; their coverage is not checked. With 80 persons, true flip rates near the margin read mostly 'undecided'. (amendment B12) The human contrast is the dataset's recording system against our replay plus our loggers, a sum; the machine contrast is no system against our system. The floor compares two kinds of absolute differences (H0 to H1 against H1 to H1_rep, sharing H1); it does not separate systematic change from replay-to-replay variation. (amendment B14) P_nohook is not taken under load. M1 against M1_replay does not separate inference load from order. The margin 0.10 is set by the sample available (n = 80 reads 'not changed' up to two flips) and tied to the validity gate's tolerance, not derived from a cost. A pair whose gap sets differ between the sides changes its judgment partly by what the detector leaves out, which is reported, not removed.
record: results/prototype_v7/record.json: counts and summaries only. record.json holds no press time, gap, key, text, LLM output text, per-person vector or person id (amendment B9: the supplement of A7 below is the only place where press times are published); ids as the SHA-256 of their sorted list. Captures of replayed KUPA series stay on the work PC and are returned only as summaries (KUPA's licence applies to anything derived). (amendment A7, the researcher's decision 6) These conditions are deposited on Zenodo with a timestamp before the first capture, after the researcher confirms the deposit, and the DOI is added. (amendment B9) The deposited version is the one after the commit of the items fixed by the work PC (fixed_before_running) and before the first capture. The recorded kinds and press times of H1, H1_rep, M3a and M3b (derived from KUPA) are published as a supplement under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 if the licence text of KUPA-KEYS allows it, checked before publication; if not, the reason is stated in the paper. (amendment B11) Those of M0, M1, M2 and P (not derived from KUPA's times) are published without that condition. L0 and L1 (the researcher's own typing) are not published.

run_order.randomised: the order of all captures is a random permutation drawn with numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 7, 6]) within blocks of one day's work, except where a series needs another first (M1_replay after its M1; L1 after L0; M2's plan before its typing); for each replay person the order of idle and load is drawn with key [20261031, 7, 7, person] (amendment B16, the researcher's decision 3) Blocks: block 0 holds L0's 4 essays (the day the researcher types); every other capture is in one of blocks 1-6, given by groups: a replay person (H1_idle, H1_load and, for the first 10, H1_rep), a text of the 8B-class model (M1_8B, M1_replay_8B, M0, M3a, M3b), a text of the 14B-class model (M1_14B, M1_replay_14B), a text of M2_8B, a text of M2_14B, a control of P (P_idle, P_load and, for 5, 18 and 50 ms, P_nohook) and an essay of L1 (L1_idle, L1_load). analysis_details.missing_judgments: a pair or session without a judgment (D3 below 70 gaps) is removed from b, c and n, and from the shares and their cluster bootstrap, and counted (amendment B14: it is a missing pair, placed back by the bounds; where a cluster holds one session, removing it from the bootstrap also removes the cluster, and the series is kept out of the general statement by the bounds in any case); judgments enter the counts only as booleans, and paired probabilities only as one-dimensional arrays of the same persons. analysis_details.across: the general statement (human side; the machine side by machine_general with B8) needs the validity of all five detectors (D1, D2_lr, D2_rf, D3, D4; D4 added by amendment B4) and a reading for each on both layers (hook, page) [the reading must be 'not changed' with all three missing-data bounds, detectors_C2.headline, amendments B11 and B12]; anything missing means no general statement is made (amendment B12; the run goes on and every cell is still reported); detectors 'not valid here' are listed apart.
analysis_details.replay_error: REVISES matching_and_cleaning and pairs.replay_error (not only a detail): drops and extras as written; the 'order inversions' are reported, in every case, as kind_edit_distance, the Levenshtein distance between the planned and recorded kind sequences (it counts inversions together with drops and extras: an adjacent swap of two kinds counts 2; a swap, drop or extra within one kind is not seen). Offset, jitter and drift are computed only when the counts are equal and the kinds agree position by position ('matched'); otherwise they are 'not evaluable', because a press missing in the middle would shift every later pair. A drop and an extra of the same kind cancel and cannot be seen (a limit). The share of captures 'matched' is reported per series.
analysis_details.resolution: Monaco's mean distance between neighbouring modes of a Gaussian KDE of press-press gaps in [0, 300] ms, evaluated on a 0.1 ms grid with a kernel SD of 1.0 ms; also taken with 0.5 ms and 2.0 ms; the estimate is read only if both lie within 10% of it ('stable'), otherwise reported as 'no resolution read'.
analysis_details.sensitivity_cleaning: after a time is changed, v6's cleaning (stable sort, a press at the same time as the previous dropped and counted) is applied with the kinds following their presses, then gaps are taken. (amendment B12, decision 32) The main analysis keeps v6's cleaning; beside it, every reading of C2 (human and machine side, both layers) is also computed with presses at the same time kept (stable sort, zero gaps retained), and the presses that v6's cleaning drops are counted per layer and series. (amendment B14, decision 36) The ties-kept version is also applied to the plan side (M1's zero gaps). (amendment B14, decision 39) For every pair, whether the set of gaps a detector uses differs between the two sides (D1's and D2's trim above 10 x the mean, D3's windows of 70, D4's first 30 press-press gaps; a pair whose numbers of gaps differ counts as differing) is recorded, and the share of pairs that differ is reported per detector, layer and side as a description of how a change came about; the headline is not changed by it.
